name: Berberine

own_problems.text: Pulled from the market in Singapore, first in 1978 — for liver harm, nerve and brain harm and blood problems

fda.text: : If pregnant or breast-feeding, ask a health professional before use. Keep out of reach of children. In case of overdose, get medical help or contact a Poison Control Center right away. Do not use if tamper evident seal is broken or missing. Store in a cool, dry place.

summary: A small computer model, rather than tests on people, gave Berberine a medium risk score of 62 for the liver and a low risk score of 37 for the heart [M]. In 1978, Singapore removed the drug from the market because of concerns over damage to the liver, harm to the brain and nerves, and blood issues [3]. The FDA warns that people who are pregnant or breast-feeding should consult a health professional before taking it, and to seek immediate medical help or call Poison Control in case of an overdose [4].
